bug_semantics: Concrete CMS Legacy Form stored XSS via unencoded multiple-choice options. MiniSurvey::loadInputType() explodes btFormQuestions.options on '%%' and concatenates each option into HTML as checkbox value/label, <option> text, and radio value/label with no HTML encoding. An authenticated user who can create or edit a Legacy Form (rogue administrator) stores a JavaScript payload in those options; concrete/blocks/form/view.php calls loadInputType() when rendering the block, so any visitor who views the page executes the payload (CWE-79). CVE.org CNA record is PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn), affected from version 5 before 9.4.8, patched in 9.4.8. Distinct from CVE-2026-3240, which is the unescaped question-label field in the same block.
flaw_origin: The flawed mechanism is missing output encoding when Legacy Form option strings are interpolated into HTML. That interpolation first appears in public history in root commit 10236caea734eeb055cd0aa18f3178bf1c6f7c0b (2008-08-04 SVN r1 initial import) in trunk/web/concrete/blocks/form/controller.php MiniSurvey::loadInputType(): select uses $html.='<option >'.trim($option).'</option>' and radios uses value=".trim($option)." /> '.$option. There is no parent commit; no finer public member of this first-write can be reconstructed (Former-commit-id f65e81cd is a rewritten duplicate root, not on 9.4.x ancestry). Checkbox-list later copied the same missing-encoding pattern in 457b64f63f43d25469ecccc3c33f3bae446521d6 (2009-01-07). Subsequent splits/moves into concrete/blocks/form/mini_survey.php and HTML/class refactors (including 507736794a form-check wrappers) preserved the unescaped interpolation until the 2026 h() fix.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-3241 / GHSA-f4vq-pj32-gr4q is a real published stored XSS in Legacy Form multiple-choice options, not a withdrawn or false advisory. The sink is MiniSurvey::loadInputType() concatenating stored option strings into checkbox, select, and radio HTML without encoding; view.php emits that HTML to any page visitor. The 9.4.8 fix is the h() wrap in c4428af, landed on 9.4.x by merge 2b75577 (PR 12826) and present in tag 9.4.8 but absent from 9.4.7, matching the vendor patched boundary. BIC search used git log -L on loadInputType through mini_survey.php and the pre-2012 form controller, plus git log -S for checkboxlist/radioPair/h($option). The smallest first-write of the unescaped option interpolation is root import 10236cae (SVN r1, 2008): select and radio option HTML are already unescaped there. That commit has no parent (introducer_parent_absent=true after direct parent-tree verification). It is a whole-tree first import, but it is also the smallest surviving public object that first wrote these lines; the Former-commit-id twin is not on 9.4.x ancestry and cannot be decomposed into finer public members. Later block delete/restore, the 2009 checkboxlist addition, the 2012 class split into form_minisurvey.php, and the 2021 form-check markup change are restore/expansion/move/refactor and are not the BIC. AI is judged only on 10236cae: human author/committer Andrew Embler in 2008, no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot marker. Verdict NOT_AI.
